blog_summary: The blog post discusses FaRM (Fast Remote Memory), a system from Microsoft Research that reimplements Facebook's TAO with remarkable performance improvements. FaRM achieves 10x higher throughput (6.3 million operations/sec per machine) and 40-50x lower latency (41µs) compared to TAO, largely due to its use of RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) over Ethernet via RoCE. The author highlights RDMA's ability to bypass kernel overhead and traditional protocol stacks, enabling low-latency, high-throughput remote memory access. FaRM provides a strictly serializable ACID programming model atop RDMA, featuring distributed transactions, lock-free reads, and data locality optimizations. The paper also details FaRM's communication primitives, distributed memory management, and transaction management, demonstrating how careful engineering can overcome RDMA's NUMA-like limitations and NIC cache constraints.
paper_abstract: We describe the design and implementation of FaRM, a new main memory distributed computing platform that exploits RDMA to improve both latency and throughput by an order of magnitude relative to state of the art main memory systems that use TCP/IP. FaRM exposes the memory of machines in the cluster as a shared address space. Applications can use transactions to allocate, read, write, and free objects in the address space with location transparency. We expect this simple programming model to be sufficient for most application code. FaRM provides two mechanisms to improve performance where required: lock-free reads over RDMA, and support for collocating objects and function shipping to enable the use of efficient single machine transactions. FaRM uses RDMA both to directly access data in the shared address space and for fast messaging and is carefully tuned for the best RDMA performance. We used FaRM to build a key-value store and a graph store similar to Facebook’s. They both perform well, for example, a 20-machine cluster can perform 167 million key-value lookups per second with a latency of 31µs.

figures.title: FaRM RDMA performance vs. TCP/IP
figures.caption: FaRM uses RDMA writes to implement a fast message passing primitive that achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in message rate and latency relative to TCP/IP on the same Ethernet network (Figure 2).
